name: g_nameHashCrc16Table
comment: 256-entry CRC-16/ARC table (reflected polynomial 0xA001, init 0) used by Str_HashName to fold the text after the '@' in a resource name into the low 16 bits of the returned name handle. Read-only; the high half of that handle carries the name-category index (BASE, ENEMY, SCENARIO_01..20, CS_01..20, ...) in bits 24..30 plus a flag bit.
evidence: Only reference in the whole image is literal 0x00157964 (ldr r2,[pc,#0x5c] at 0x00157900) inside Str_HashName (0x001577FC). The loop 0x00157908..0x00157928 is the standard reflected CRC-16 update: ldrb r3,[r0],#1; eor ip,r3,r1; and ip,ip,#0xff; add ip,r2,ip,lsl #1; ldrh ip,[ip]; eor r1,ip,r1,lsr #8, with crc cleared by mov r1,#0 at 0x001578F4 and ORed into the low half of the return value at 0x0015792C..0x00157934. The 512 bytes at 0x007275F4..0x007277F4 are exactly the 256-entry CRC-16/ARC (IBM) table (0x0000,0xC0C1,0xC181,0x0140,...,0x4040), verified by regenerating it with polynomial 0xA001; the next object at 0x007277F4 is the float 2.0f, so the extent is 512 bytes. The hashed bytes are the part of the name after the '@' separator: the string "@" sits at 0x0015795C (add r1,pc,#0xec at 0x00157868), strstr (0x001009B4) finds it, the buffer is truncated there (strb r6,[r0,r5] at 0x00157890) and the CRC starts at name+offset+1 (add r0,r8,r5; ldrb r2,[r0,#1]! at 0x001578F0).
